incidents.vector: Breached a public API endpoint, then used autonomous AI agents to map the network, raid source repositories, seize root credentials and hijack CI/CD pipelines and cloud AI infrastructure.
incidents.impact: Weeks of intrusion tradecraft compressed into under 10 hours; attacker stole credentials and cloud keys, established redundant persistence, and used the victim's own AI endpoints as attack infrastructure before demanding ransom.

incidents.vector: Exploits poorly secured VPNs and remote-access tools, internet-facing application flaws, and credentials stolen from business partners; deploys custom ransomware, loader, RAT and security-software killer.
incidents.impact: At least seven Russian organizations hit with custom ransomware and multimillion-dollar ransom demands; stolen data may also be published or reused in further operations against Russian entities.

incidents.vector: Commercial spyware delivered via a zero-click iPhone exploit and via physical device access during police detention and questioning.
incidents.impact: 14 people targeted, including a member of parliament, in the largest documented spyware wave in Serbia to date; infections confirmed on activist devices ahead of March local and October parliamentary elections.

incidents.vector: Exploitation of CVE-2026-82329, a critical unauthenticated authentication-bypass in default Artifactory configurations, within three days of disclosure; public proof-of-concept now available.
incidents.impact: Attackers are minting administrator tokens and enumerating users, credentials and federated access on exposed instances; admin access to a central artifact repository enables software supply chain tampering across some 6,600 customer organizations.

incidents.vector: Apparent long-running, still-active breach of a Louisiana-based identity verification provider whose scanners are used by rental car firms, dispensaries, hotels and retailers.
incidents.impact: A dark-web service called Nexus is selling scans of 153M+ US and Canadian driver's licenses, including those of senior US officials, with roughly 400,000 new records added in 24 hours; the FBI has opened an inquiry.

incidents.vector: Intrusion into company servers with exfiltration of patient, employee, provider and financial data; a Russia-based ransomware-as-a-service gang claimed the attack.
incidents.impact: Operator of 27 hospitals and outpatient facilities in 12 states is being extorted with threats to leak stolen data; a class action lawsuit has already been filed over the breach.

incidents.vector: Compromise of Cisco IOS XR routers, TACACS authentication servers and management infrastructure with custom router malware, traffic capture and log tampering.
incidents.impact: Attackers harvested credentials in transit, monitored administrative activity, and used compromised network infrastructure as a vantage point to pivot into connected high-value and critical infrastructure environments.

incidents.vector: OAuth consent phishing over a commercial messaging app: attackers impersonate officials and journalists and trick targets into granting a malicious application persistent access to Microsoft or Google accounts.
incidents.impact: Grants attackers long-term access to email and files that survives password changes and bypasses MFA; FBI issued a public alert on the campaign, which it has tracked since late 2025.

incidents.vector: Exploited a vulnerability in the Cosmos blockchain platform that had also been used the prior week to steal from six other platforms.
incidents.impact: Attacker initially made off with about $74 million in crypto assets; roughly $68 million was clawed back within hours and Cosmos halted all activity pending remediation.

incidents.vector: ClickFix social engineering via compromised websites and fake Cloudflare verification overlays, installing a backdoor that retrieves its command-and-control address from the Polygon blockchain.
incidents.impact: At least 31 organizations compromised with persistent backdoors that survive C2 takedowns, since the attacker can repoint infected machines to new servers via blockchain transactions for fractions of a cent.

incidents.vector: 20-year-old polymorphic file-infecting malware forming a peer-to-peer botnet used to distribute payloads, including a clipboard hijacker that swapped cryptocurrency wallet addresses.
incidents.impact: CrowdStrike, DOJ, FBI, Europol and partners sinkholed the botnet on Aug 31, cutting the operator off from 15,000+ machines; the operator had stolen at least ~$150K in crypto plus other revenue streams. Infected hosts now beacon to defender-run sinkholes.

incidents.vector: External Microsoft Teams accounts posing as IT help desks initiate voice calls that coerce employees into running remote-management tools or malware; one variant escalated to an NTLM relay attack against domain controllers.
incidents.impact: Coordinated January–April 2026 operation targeted more than 150 employees across at least 10 companies, attempting to gain remote control of endpoints and domain-level privileges.

incidents.vector: ClickFix-style fake CAPTCHA pages trick users into pasting a malicious command into PowerShell, triggering DLL sideloading, payloads hidden in PNG images and a Python-based reverse-tunnel implant.
incidents.impact: Reverse tunnels give attackers direct access into internal networks, enabling privilege escalation, data exfiltration and ransomware deployment; Microsoft flagged the campaign as a serious enterprise threat.

incidents.vector: Active exploitation of two PaperCut print-management vulnerabilities: a missing-authentication flaw (CVE-2026-81578) and an unsafe reflection flaw (CVE-2026-82078).
incidents.impact: CISA added both flaws to the Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog and directed federal agencies to prioritize remediation; organizations running exposed PaperCut servers face compromise risk.

incidents.vector: 33-hour BGP hijack of part of Hetzner's address space let the attacker obtain a valid TLS certificate, clone the vendor's site and serve malicious updates for the Virtualizor VPS management platform.
incidents.impact: Unknown number of hosting providers received malicious software updates; traffic and possibly payment data passed exclusively through attacker infrastructure, leaving the vendor unable to assess the full scope.

incidents.vector: Manipulated the platform's token prices to borrow assets with no collateral.
incidents.impact: $8.7 million in crypto assets stolen — the platform's fourth hack in twelve months; all borrowing paused during investigation.

incidents.vector: Distributed denial-of-service attack against government network infrastructure.
incidents.impact: Norway's government network was temporarily taken down; a pro-Kremlin hacktivist group claimed responsibility.

incidents.vector: Social engineering / identity abuse against third-party applications, with a four-day data theft window (Aug 21–25) before discovery.
incidents.impact: Data on oncology, multispecialty and medical-surgical customers stolen from the distributor of roughly one-third of North American pharmaceuticals; extortionists reportedly demand over $55 million with intermittent service degradation reported.

incidents.vector: Network intrusion into two Berlin ministries between Aug 7–12 with large-scale data exfiltration, followed by an extortion demand.
incidents.impact: Attackers claim 5.79 TB of government data including contracts, emails and classified material, auctioned for ~$2.3M; Berlin refused to pay. Two ministries were cut off from the state network, disrupting some public services weeks before elections.

incidents.victim: Gov & defense orgs in Romania, Spain, Türkiye
incidents.vector: Spearphishing with macro-enabled Word documents using diplomatic lures, deploying a lightweight batch-script backdoor that abuses legitimate webhook services for command-and-control.
incidents.impact: Initial-access campaigns from September 2025 to April 2026 against European government, diplomatic and defense manufacturing targets, consistent with intelligence collection around Moldova's elections and NATO-adjacent governance.

incidents.vector: Malicious code embedded in hundreds of open-source packages and a self-propagating worm that stole developer credentials to compromise further repositories.
incidents.impact: Australian Federal Police arrested two men, aged 21 and 23, tied to the group blamed for the longest-running software supply chain attack spree on record, which extorted thousands of businesses worldwide.

incidents.victim: Web servers in Brazil, Bolivia, China, Canada, Vietnam
incidents.attacker: Criminal gang — Chinese-speaking, SEO fraud and data theft
incidents.vector: AI-assisted exploitation of known vulnerabilities in internet-facing Windows and Linux web servers at scale, followed by privilege escalation, rootkits and a custom cross-platform backdoor with EDR-killing capability.
incidents.impact: Compromised servers across five countries were monetized through SEO fraud and data theft, working from a target list of roughly 170,000 URLs; the group is increasingly using AI to build its malware and automate intrusions.

incidents.vector: Near-autonomous multi-agent AI attack using up to eight coordinated AI agents for reconnaissance, credential cracking, vulnerability exploitation and backdoor installation across 12 attack waves.
incidents.impact: Government agencies, most likely in Taiwan, were compromised over four days in July with personnel records exfiltrated and persistent backdoors installed on government web applications — described as the first near-autonomous AI attack on a nation-state.
